questions.question_text:
A magician draws one card from each of two different decks. The draws are independent, and each card is red or black.
The probability of a red card from deck $1$ is $0.25$.
The probability of a red card from deck $2$ is twice the probability of a red card from deck $1$.
What is the probability of drawing a red card from deck $1$ and a black card from deck $2$?

options.why: Used $0.25$ for the probability of black from deck $2$, giving $0.25 \times 0.25 = 0.0625$.
Added $0.25$ and $0.5$ instead of multiplying the probabilities along the path.

questions.solution_text:
$P(\text{red from deck }2) = 2 \times 0.25$
$= 0.5$
$P(\text{black from deck }2) = 1 - 0.5$
$= 0.5$
$P(\text{red then black}) = 0.25 \times 0.5$
$= 0.125$

questions.question_text:
Amira makes a free throw $\frac{2}{5}$ of the time, and her shots are independent.
She takes three free throws.
What is the probability that she makes exactly two of them?

Found the probability of making exactly one shot instead of exactly two.

questions.solution_text:
$P(MMX) = \frac{2}{5} \times \frac{2}{5} \times \frac{3}{5}$
$= \frac{12}{125}$
The missed shot could be the first, second or third, so three paths each have probability $\frac{12}{125}$.
$P(\text{exactly two made}) = 3 \times \frac{12}{125}$
$= \frac{36}{125}$
